322	def profile(crossings, tolerances):
323	    """Build a tolerance profile from :func:`audit` results.
324	
325	    Calls :func:`audit` exactly once with ``crossings`` and
326	    ``tolerances``, so its validation, first-error order, exceptions
327	    (propagated unchanged) and index prefixes all apply here as well.
328	    Inputs are not modified.
329	
330	    With ``R`` the tuple returned by :func:`audit`, one item per input
331	    tolerance, items are ordered ascending by
332	    ``(tolerances[i], i)``; equal tolerances therefore keep their input
333	    order. ``curve`` is a tuple of dicts, one per ordered item, each
334	    with keys in the order
335	    ``tolerance, within_tolerance, within_ratio, bias, rmse,
336	    quality``; ``tolerance`` is ``round(float(tolerances[i]), 6)``
337	    (negative zero normalized to ``0.0``) and the remaining fields are
338	    copied unchanged from the corresponding ``R`` item.
339	
340	    ``monotonic`` is whether the ``within_tolerance`` counts are
341	    non-decreasing along the curve (``True`` for a single item).
342	    ``first_pass_tolerance`` is the rounded threshold of the first
343	    curve item whose ``quality`` is ``"pass"``, or ``None`` when no
344	    item passes.
345	
346	    With ``t_i`` the *unrounded* tolerance and ``q_i`` the
347	    ``within_ratio`` of the item at ordered position ``i`` and
348	    ``m = len(R)``, ``area`` is ``0.0`` for ``m < 2`` and otherwise the
349	    trapezoidal integral
350	    ``round(float(fsum((t_i - t_{i-1}) * (q_i + q_{i-1}) / 2
351	    for i in range(1, m))), 6)`` with negative zero normalized to
352	    ``0.0``.
353	
354	    Returns a dict with keys in the order
355	    ``curve, monotonic, first_pass_tolerance, area``; their types are
356	    tuple, bool, float or ``None`` and float.
357	    """
358	    reports = audit(crossings, tolerances)
359	    return _profile_from_reports(reports, tolerances)

362	def _aggregate_from_reports(reports, tolerances):
363	    """Compute the :func:`aggregate` result from an :func:`audit` tuple."""
364	    m = len(reports)
365	
366	    count = sum(x["count"] for x in reports)
367	    pass_count = sum(x["quality"] == "pass" for x in reports)
368	    fail_count = m - pass_count
369	    mean_bias = math.fsum(x["bias"] for x in reports) / m
370	    max_rmse = max(x["rmse"] for x in reports)
371	    mean_ratio = math.fsum(x["within_ratio"] for x in reports) / m
372	
373	    passed = [t for t, x in zip(tolerances, reports) if x["quality"] == "pass"]
374	    best_tolerance = min(passed) if passed else None
375	
376	    result = {
377	        "count": int(count),
378	        "pass_count": int(pass_count),
379	        "fail_count": int(fail_count),
380	    }
381	    for name, value in (
382	        ("mean_bias", mean_bias),
383	        ("max_rmse", max_rmse),
384	        ("mean_ratio", mean_ratio),
385	    ):
386	        value = round(float(value), 6)
387	        result[name] = 0.0 if value == 0 else value
388	    if best_tolerance is None:
389	        result["best_tolerance"] = None
390	    else:
391	        best_tolerance = round(float(best_tolerance), 6)
392	        result["best_tolerance"] = 0.0 if best_tolerance == 0 else best_tolerance
393	    result["quality"] = "pass" if pass_count == m else "fail"
394	    return result

426	def dashboard(crossings, tolerances):
427	    """Bundle :func:`audit`, :func:`profile` and :func:`aggregate` results.
428	
429	    Calls :func:`audit` exactly once with ``crossings`` and
430	    ``tolerances``, so its validation, first-error order, exceptions
431	    (propagated unchanged) and index prefixes all apply here as well.
432	    Inputs are not modified; :func:`profile` and :func:`aggregate` are
433	    not called (their values are derived directly from the single
434	    :func:`audit` result).

457	def dashboard_summary(crossings, tolerances):
458	    """Summarize crosspoint depth differences across tolerances.
459	
460	    ``crossings`` is a non-empty list/tuple; each item is a
461	    four-element list/tuple ``(x, y, d1, d2)`` whose fields are finite
462	    non-bool int/float values, with ``d1, d2 >= 0``. ``tolerances``
463	    must then be a non-empty list/tuple whose items, checked in input
464	    order, are finite non-bool int/float values ``> 0``.
465	
466	    Validation order (first error wins): the ``crossings`` container,
467	    its non-emptiness, each crossing in index order (item container,
468	    length, fields), then the ``tolerances`` container, its
469	    non-emptiness, then each tolerance in index order (type,
470	    finiteness, positivity). Type mismatches raise ``TypeError``; every
471	    other violation raises ``ValueError``. Item errors are prefixed
472	    with ``"crossings[i]: "`` or ``"tolerances[i]: "``.
473	
474	    With ``r = d1 - d2``, ``n`` the number of crosspoints and each
475	    tolerance ``t``, the per-tolerance statistics are
476	    ``b = fsum(r) / n`` (mean bias), ``e = sqrt(fsum(r**2) / n)``
477	    (RMSE), ``w`` the number of crosspoints with ``abs(r) <= t`` and
478	    ``q = w / n``; the tolerance passes (``p``) when ``w == n``.
479	
480	    Returns a dict with keys in the order
481	    ``count, pass_count, fail_count, total_count, mean_bias, max_rmse,
482	    mean_ratio, quality``; ``count`` is the number of tolerances;
483	    ``pass_count``/``fail_count`` are the numbers of tolerances for
484	    which ``p`` is true/false; ``total_count`` is the sum of ``n`` over
485	    the tolerances; ``mean_bias`` is the mean of the ``b`` values,
486	    ``max_rmse`` the maximum of the ``e`` values and ``mean_ratio`` the
487	    mean of the ``q`` values; ``quality`` is ``"pass"`` only when every
488	    tolerance passes and ``"fail"`` otherwise. Counts are ints and the
489	    statistics are floats rounded to 6 decimals (negative zero
490	    normalized to ``0.0``). Inputs are not modified.
491	    """
492	    _validate_crossings(crossings)
493	    _validate_tolerances(tolerances)
494	
495	    differences = [d1 - d2 for x, y, d1, d2 in crossings]
496	    n = len(differences)
497	    m = len(tolerances)
498	
499	    biases = []
500	    rmses = []
501	    ratios = []
502	    pass_count = 0
503	    for tolerance in tolerances:
504	        bias = math.fsum(differences) / n
505	        rmse = math.sqrt(math.fsum(r * r for r in differences) / n)
506	        within = sum(1 for r in differences if abs(r) <= tolerance)
507	        biases.append(bias)
508	        rmses.append(rmse)
509	        ratios.append(within / n)
510	        if within == n:
511	            pass_count += 1
512	
513	    fail_count = m - pass_count
514	    mean_bias = math.fsum(biases) / m
515	    max_rmse = max(rmses)
516	    mean_ratio = math.fsum(ratios) / m
517	
518	    result = {
519	        "count": int(m),
520	        "pass_count": int(pass_count),
521	        "fail_count": int(fail_count),
522	        "total_count": int(n * m),
523	    }
524	    for name, value in (
525	        ("mean_bias", mean_bias),
526	        ("max_rmse", max_rmse),
527	        ("mean_ratio", mean_ratio),
528	    ):
529	        value = round(float(value), 6)
530	        result[name] = 0.0 if value == 0 else value
531	    result["quality"] = "pass" if pass_count == m else "fail"
532	    return result
533

576	    best_tolerance = min(passed) if passed else None
577	
578	    quality_score = 100 * (pass_count / m) * mean_ratio
579	
580	    summary = {
581	        "count": int(m),
582	        "pass_count": int(pass_count),
583	        "fail_count": int(fail_count),
584	        "total_count": int(total_count),
585	    }
586	    for name, value in (
587	        ("mean_bias", mean_bias),
588	        ("max_rmse", max_rmse),
589	        ("mean_ratio", mean_ratio),
590	    ):
591	        value = round(float(value), 6)
592	        summary[name] = 0.0 if value == 0 else value
593	    if best_tolerance is None:
594	        summary["best_tolerance"] = None
595	    else:
596	        best_tolerance = round(float(best_tolerance), 6)
597	        summary["best_tolerance"] = 0.0 if best_tolerance == 0 else best_tolerance
598	    quality_score = round(float(quality_score), 6)
599	    summary["quality_score"] = 0.0 if quality_score == 0 else quality_score
600	
601	    return {
602	        "dashboard": result,
603	        "summary": summary,
604	        "quality": result[3],

608	def gate(crossings, tolerances, min_mean_ratio=1.0, max_rmse_limit=1.0):
609	    """Gate a :func:`dashboard_report` against summary thresholds.
610	
611	    Calls :func:`dashboard_report` exactly once with ``crossings`` and
612	    ``tolerances``, so its validation, first-error order, exceptions
613	    (propagated unchanged) and index prefixes all apply here as well.
614	    Inputs and the :func:`dashboard_report` result are not modified.
615	
616	    The thresholds are then validated in order: first
617	    ``min_mean_ratio``, then ``max_rmse_limit``. Each must be a finite
618	    non-bool int/float; ``min_mean_ratio`` must lie in ``[0, 1]`` and
619	    ``max_rmse_limit`` must be ``>= 0``. Type mismatches raise
620	    ``TypeError``; non-finite or out-of-range values raise
621	    ``ValueError``.
622	
623	    With ``D`` the dict returned by :func:`dashboard_report` and
624	    ``S = D["summary"]``, returns a dict with keys in the order
625	    ``report, checks, quality``. ``report`` is ``D`` itself.
626	    ``checks`` is a dict with keys in the order ``mean_ratio, max_rmse,
627	    within_ok, rmse_ok``; the first two are the floats
628	    ``S["mean_ratio"]`` and ``S["max_rmse"]``, and the last two are the
629	    bools ``S["mean_ratio"] >= min_mean_ratio`` and
630	    ``S["max_rmse"] <= max_rmse_limit``. ``quality`` is ``"pass"`` only
631	    when ``D["quality"]`` is ``"pass"`` and both checks are true, and
632	    ``"fail"`` otherwise.
633	    """
634	    result = dashboard_report(crossings, tolerances)

712	def pair(first, second, tolerance=1.0):
713	    """Pair points from two surveys at coincident locations.
714	
715	    ``first`` and ``second`` are non-empty lists/tuples of points; each
716	    point is a three-element list/tuple ``(x, y, d)`` whose fields are
717	    finite non-bool int/float values, with ``d >= 0``. ``tolerance``
718	    must be a finite non-bool int/float ``> 0``.
719	
720	    Each ``first`` point is processed in input order and matched to the
721	    still-unused ``second`` point minimizing the unrounded 2-D distance
722	    ``sqrt((x1 - x2)**2 + (y1 - y2)**2)``, provided it does not exceed
723	    ``tolerance``; equal distances resolve to the earliest ``second``
724	    point in input order. A ``first`` point with no admissible match is
725	    skipped, and a ``second`` point can be used at most once. If fewer
726	    than one pair is formed, a ``ValueError`` is raised.
727	
728	    Validation order (first error wins): the ``first`` container, its
729	    non-emptiness, the ``second`` container, its non-emptiness, each
730	    point in index order (first ``first`` points then ``second`` points:
731	    point container, length, fields), then ``tolerance`` (type,
732	    finiteness, positivity). Point errors are prefixed with
733	    ``"first[i]: "`` or ``"second[j]: "``.
734	
735	    Returns a tuple, in ``first`` input order, of four-element tuples
736	    ``(x, y, d1, d2)`` whose items are all floats; ``x``/``y`` and
737	    ``d1`` come from the ``first`` point and ``d2`` from the matched
738	    ``second`` point. Values are rounded to 6 decimals (negative zero
739	    normalized to ``0.0``). Inputs are not modified.
740	    """
741	    if not isinstance(first, (list, tuple)):
742	        raise TypeError("first must be a list or tuple")
743	    if len(first) == 0:
744	        raise ValueError("first must be non-empty")
745	    if not isinstance(second, (list, tuple)):
746	        raise TypeError("second must be a list or tuple")
747	    if len(second) == 0:
748	        raise ValueError("second must be non-empty")
749	
750	    for label, points in (("first", first), ("second", second)):
751	        for i in range(len(points)):
752	            point = points[i]
753	            prefix = f"{label}[{i}]: "
754	            if not isinstance(point, (list, tuple)):
755	                raise TypeError(prefix + "must be a list or tuple")
756	            if len(point) != 3:
757	                raise ValueError(prefix + "must have 3 elements")
758	            for name, value in zip(_POINT_FIELDS, point):
759	                if not _is_real_number(value):
760	                    raise TypeError(prefix + f"{name} must be a non-bool int or float")
761	            for name, value in zip(_POINT_FIELDS, point):
762	                if not math.isfinite(value):
763	                    raise ValueError(prefix + f"{name} must be finite")
764	            if not point[2] >= 0:
765	                raise ValueError(prefix + "d must be >= 0")
766	
767	    if not _is_real_number(tolerance):
768	        raise TypeError("tolerance must be a non-bool int or float")
769	    if not math.isfinite(tolerance):
770	        raise ValueError("tolerance must be finite")
771	    if not tolerance > 0:
772	        raise ValueError("tolerance must be > 0")
773	
774	    used = [False] * len(second)
775	    pairs = []
776	    for x1, y1, d1 in first:
777	        best_index = None
778	        best_distance = None
779	        for j in range(len(second)):
780	            if used[j]:
781	                continue
782	            x2, y2, d2 = second[j]
783	            distance = math.sqrt((x1 - x2) ** 2 + (y1 - y2) ** 2)
784	            if distance <= tolerance and (
785	                best_distance is None or distance < best_distance
786	            ):
787	                best_index = j
788	                best_distance = distance
789	        if best_index is None:
790	            continue
791	        used[best_index] = True
792	        x2, y2, d2 = second[best_index]
793	        pairs.append((x1, y1, d1, d2))
794	
795	    if len(pairs) == 0:
796	        raise ValueError("no points matched within tolerance")
797	
798	    result = []
799	    for x, y, d1, d2 in pairs:
800	        item = []
801	        for value in (x, y, d1, d2):
802	            rounded = round(float(value), 6)
803	            item.append(0.0 if rounded == 0 else rounded)
804	        result.append(tuple(item))
805	    return tuple(result)

1594	    and ``quality`` must be ``"pass"`` or ``"fail"``. Writing ``n`` for
